item.title: Read to a Dog — Wed Nov 25, 2:00 PM — Petaluma Regional Library
item.description:

Children build confidence in their reading skills by reading aloud in a safe space. Ven a leer en voz alta a los perros de PALS \(Paws as Loving Support\). Estos perros son bien entrenados y les encantan escuchar cuentos en inglés y español. Los niños desarrollan confianza en sus habilidades de lectura leyendo en voz alta en un espacio seguro.

Book Club titles and dates are subject to change. sonomalibrary.org/bookclubs 2026 Schedule January 28 - The Midnight Library by Matt Haig February 25 - The Savage Kind by John Copenhaver March 25 - It Rhymes with Takei by George Takei April 29 - The Thirty Names of Night by Zeyn Joukhadar May 27 - The Antique Hunter's Guide to Murder by C.L. Miller June 24 - The Stonewall Reader Edited by the NY Public Library July 29 - River Sing Me Home by Eleanor Shearer August 26 - How to Solve your own Murder by Kristen Perrin September 30 - The Wide Wide Sea by Hampton Sides October 28 - Love After the End by Joshua Whitehead November 25 - The Bad Muslim Discount by Syed M. Masood
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Turkey Waddle Hike 2026 — Fri Nov 27, 10:00 AM — Jack London State Historic Park
item.description:
Skip the shopping crowds and spend the day after Thanksgiving enjoying the great outdoors! Join us for a refreshing guided hike through the park’s beautiful mixed evergreen forests to the majestic Ancient Redwood. Bring family and friends, enjoy some fresh air, and discover a little post-holiday magic along the trail. This moderate, approximately 3.5-mile round-trip hike leads to an old-growth coast redwood that stood here long before Jack London arrived, and continues to stand as a living link
Source: Jack London State Historic Park

item.title: Holiday Tree Lighting with Winemaker James MacPhail at Region — Fri Nov 27, 4:00 PM — Region.
item.description:
Kick off the holiday season with us at Region! Join us for a festive afternoon of exceptional Sonoma County wines, delicious holiday bites, and a little holiday magic.
We are so excited to have special guest Winemaker James MacPhail of Tongue Dancer Wines joining us for the celebration! With over 30 years of winemaking experience, James is one of Sonoma County's most celebrated Pinot Noir & Chardonnay producers. His passion, personality, and deep Sonoma roots make him the perfect guest to help us toast the season!
Sip on his incredible wines, enjoy festive holiday bites, and gather around our towering 23-foot Christmas tree as James leads a celebratory toast to officially kickoff the holiday season.
🎄 A Special Tree Lighting Toast – Raise a glass with James MacPhail as we light up the tree at 5:30pm!
🍷 Featured Wines & Holiday Bites – Enjoy special pours from Tongue Dancer Wines alongside delicious seasonal bites.
🎁 Mystery Bottle Wine Sale – Feeling lucky? Purchase a $40 mystery

item.title: Disability Support Hour — Tue Dec 1, 1:00 PM — Disability Cultural Center - 3rd Floor Landing
item.description:
This is a weekly meetup for disabled people and allies to come together and find support and community, ask questions, or just talk through whatever they may be going through! Sometimes there is a topic or guest speaker, or we talk about whatever we feel like bringing up that week! We also have one of our DCC therapy dogs, Casper, with us too! We meet every Tuesday from 1:00pm to 2:00pm in the Disability Cultural Center on the 3rd-floor landing of the SRJC Bertolini Student Center. Come and check it out!For more information, visit SRJC's DCC website. (https://drd.santarosa.edu/dcc)
Source: Santa Rosa Junior College

item.title: Therapy Dog Wellness Hour — Tue Dec 1, 1:00 PM — Disability Cultural Center - 3rd Floor Landing
item.description:
Meet the DCC Therapy Dogs! Bear, Casper, and Riley are here to help you de-stress and regulate during your busy week! Riley (on left) visits on Mondays from 10:30am to 11:30am Casper (on right) visits on Tuesdays from 1:00pm to 2:00pm Bear (in center) visits on Wednesdays from 11:30am to 12:30pm That's THREE days of Therapy dogs in the DCC! Visit us on the third-floor landing of Bertolini to meet our Therapy Dogs and checkout all the other cool stuff we have going on!For more information, visit SRJC's DCC website. (https://drd.santarosa.edu/dcc)
Source: Santa Rosa Junior College

item.description:

Tuesdays | 2:30pm to 3:30pm Thursdays | 2:30pm to 3:30pm In the Disability Cultural Center (3rd floor landing, Bertolini Student Center)For more information, visit the Disability Cultural Center website. item.title: Sistah 2 Sistah — Tue Dec 1, 4:00 PM — Pioneer Hall
item.description:

(https://bloc.santarosa.edu/august-2026) Sistah 2 Sistah is a welcoming space for Black girls and young women to connect, uplift, and empower one another. Through sisterhood, conversation, wellness, education, leadership, and creative experiences, students can build meaningful relationships while growing personally and academically. Topics and activities may include:Sisterhood & community Self-love and confidence Academic & career success Wellness and life skills Leadership and personal growth Cultural identity and self-discovery The Sawubona BLOC is located in Pioneer Hall, Room 360 (next to the bookstore) on the Santa Rosa Campus.

item.title: Santa Paws - Pictures with Santa for Dogs and Cats — Sun Dec 6, 11:00 AM — Barber Lee Spirits
item.description:
Santa is at the distillery, and he's taking pictures with dogs and cats. Bring yours to Barber Lee Spirits Distillery on Sunday, December 6, from 11 am to 2 pm. Cats may have opinions about this. Bring them anyway.
The event is in partnership with Sage Compassion for Animals, a Bay Area nonprofit that helps families pay for veterinary care when a pet is in a medical crisis. When a dog or cat needs emergency treatment and the bill is more than a family can cover, SageC4A steps in so the pet gets care and stays home with the people who love it. They also teach pet owners how to prevent illness before it becomes an emergency.
A portion of the day's proceeds goes to that work. SageC4A will be on site to answer questions, with a donation jar and QR codes if you'd like to give more.
Barber Lee makes spirits, but there's also wine, non-alcoholic drinks, food, chocolate, and cheese. Kids are welcome. Stay a while.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
